claim_verdicts.claim_text: The confirmed pathogen is Streptococcus pneumoniae.

citations.quote: Assessment: right lower lobe pneumonia, likely Streptococcus pneumoniae.
2026-01-20 21:00 | urine Streptococcus pneumoniae antigen | ordered; specimen not received by laboratory as of 2026-01-22 10:00
Plan: two sets of blood cultures and a sputum culture; urine Streptococcus pneumoniae antigen; ceftriaxone 1 g IV and azithromycin 500 mg IV; admit to medicine.
Impression: community-acquired pneumonia of the right lower lobe; presentation suggestive of pneumococcal pneumonia.
2026-01-21 09:15 | sputum Gram stain | specimen rejected: more than 25 squamous epithelial cells per low-power field (oropharyngeal contamination); recollection requested
2026-01-22 07:00 | blood culture sets 1 and 2 | preliminary report: no growth at 36 hours; final report pending (5-day incubation)

claim_verdicts.why: The chart only describes Streptococcus pneumoniae as a likely pathogen, and the urine antigen test that would address it was ordered but its specimen had not been received by the laboratory. Nothing shown confirms the pathogen, so calling it confirmed is not supported.
claim_verdicts.uncertainty: The cited Hospital Day 3 note and sputum findings were not among the lines shown, and the urine antigen result is absent from the chart excerpt, so confirmation cannot be established from these lines.

claim_verdicts.claim_text: The Hospital Day 3 assessment documents pneumococcal pneumonia.

citations.quote: Assessment: pneumococcal pneumonia, improving.

claim_verdicts.why: The Hospital Day 3 progress note (2026-01-22 09:40) states the assessment as pneumococcal pneumonia, which is exactly what the claim says the document documents.
claim_verdicts.uncertainty: The claim concerns only what the Day 3 note says; the chart elsewhere holds a preliminary 'likely' or 'suggestive' wording and blood cultures are not final, but these do not affect whether the note says it.

citations.quote: History: three days of fever, cough productive of rust-colored sputum, and right-sided pleuritic chest pain.

claim_verdicts.why: The 2026-01-20 19:15 ED history line P005 explicitly records a cough productive of rust-colored sputum, directly supporting the claim as a reported finding.
claim_verdicts.uncertainty: The sputum appearance is a patient-reported history item; the sputum culture was rejected for contamination and recollection was not received, so no microbiologic confirmation exists, but the claim concerns the reported sputum color only.

claim_verdicts.claim_text: The patient has lobar consolidation on chest X-ray.

citations.quote: Findings: dense consolidation in the right lower lobe with air bronchograms. No pleural effusion. No pneumothorax.

claim_verdicts.why: The radiology finding R005 describes dense right lower lobe consolidation with air bronchograms, which the claim of lobar consolidation on chest X-ray matches. The impression R006 also describes right lower lobe consolidation.
claim_verdicts.uncertainty: The record describes a single-lobe (right lower lobe) consolidation; the word 'lobar' is a reasonable description of that finding but the report does not use the term itself.

claim_verdicts.claim_text: The pneumonia diagnosis is consistent with the classic rust-colored sputum.

citations.quote: History: three days of fever, cough productive of rust-colored sputum, and right-sided pleuritic chest pain.

claim_verdicts.why: The emergency note records a productive cough with rust-colored sputum [P005] alongside an impression of community-acquired right lower lobe pneumonia [P007]. The claim that the diagnosis is consistent with this symptom is what the lines show, and it does not assert a confirmed pathogen.
claim_verdicts.uncertainty: The sputum culture was rejected for contamination [L009], so the causative organism is not confirmed by the record.

citations.quote: Clinically improving; tolerating diet; SpO2 96% on room air.
Improving; afebrile since 04:00. SpO2 95% on 2 L/min nasal cannula.

claim_verdicts.why: The 2026-01-22 progress note (P014) states the patient is clinically improving, and an earlier note (P010) also records improvement. The claim is stated at the same level of certainty as the notes.
claim_verdicts.uncertainty: Improvement is clinical and based on a single day's note; the cited plan line P012 itself does not state improvement and is only context.

claim_verdicts.claim_text: The patient is receiving ceftriaxone and azithromycin.

citations.quote: Plan: continue ceftriaxone and azithromycin; follow up cultures and urine antigen.

claim_verdicts.why: The 2026-01-21 plan line [P012] says to continue ceftriaxone and azithromycin, and the later 2026-01-22 note [P014] documents clinical improvement on that therapy. P008 also shows both drugs were started on admission.
claim_verdicts.uncertainty: The record shows a plan to continue the drugs as of 01-21 and improvement on 01-22; it does not include a medication administration record confirming doses given on 01-22.
